title: View of the Hebrews; exhibiting the destruction of Jerusalem (1st ed.)
author: Ethan Smith
evidence: Printed Poultney, Vt.: Smith & Shute, 1823. Advertised and reviewed 1823-1824 in Vermont and eastern New York (Poultney Gazette 10 Dec 1823; Saratoga Sentinel 23 and 30 Dec 1823; Ballston Spa Gazette 20 Apr 1824), per the sourced B. H. Roberts Foundation timeline. No Palmyra, Ontario or Wayne County ad found; the Wayne Sentinel OCR has no hit for the title (OCR misses are not negatives). Indirect only: Josiah Priest's Wonders of Nature and Providence (Albany 1825), which reprints VOTH ch. 3, is Manchester Library no. 208 but Paul documents its circulation only 'by late 1836'. Grunder MP 398 (pp. 1619-20) adds a long favourable review of this first edition in The Utica Christian Repository 4:5 (May 1825), pp. 143-49, printed by William Williams of Utica; checked on the Internet Archive scan (heading 'View of the Hebrews; by Ethan Smith ... Poultney: Smith & Shute. 12mo. pp. 183.' = the 1823 edition). A review published in central New York meets the stated rule for 2; rescored 1 -> 2 on 2026-11-06. Grunder also cites the Manchester holding of Priest's Wonders (MP 341, p. 1323), which we had from Paul. No hit in the Ontario Repository OCR, 1824-1826 (not a negative).

title: The Late War, between the United States and Great Britain
author: Gilbert J. Hunt
evidence: Printed New York: Longworth 1816; reissued 1817 and 1819 as 'The Historical Reader' (Grunder MP 193: fourteen 1819 issues, none after). No ad, sale or holding naming Hunt found near Palmyra. Palmyra 'Historical Reader' ads 1827-1830 (Wayne Sentinel; read on the scans) never name an author. The one 'Historical Reader' with a named author in these papers is J. L. Blake's (Ontario Repository, Canandaigua, 28 Dec 1825 p1, page view). Canandaigua Bookstore sold an unnamed 'History of the late War' (Ontario Repository 22 Sep 1824 p3, page view), a title also used by Brackenridge and Gilleland (1817, in our catalog), so unassignable. The recurring 1825-26 'late war between the United States and Great Britain' is a chronology added to Walker's dictionary, not Hunt. Not in Strong's 1818/1819 Palmyra lists; no Hunt title in the Palmyra Register (1817-21) or Herald (1822-23) OCR; a 9 Aug 1820 Register piece mocks a different 'History of the late war' (Hartford 1815). Grunder treats it as a style parallel only. Would be 3 only if a local ad were shown to be Hunt's. Detail: docs/access-evidence.md.

Gilleland's History of the Late War between the United States and Great Britain, both from 1817 and in our catalog), so unassignable; 28 Dec 1825 p1, Bemis, Morse & Ward's 'New School Books' lists 'Historical Reader, for the use of [schools a]nd families, on a new plan. By [J. L.] Blake' -- the only 'Historical Reader' in these papers that names an author is Blake's; and the recurring 1825-26 'late war between the United States and Great Britain' is the chronological table added to a Canandaigua edition of Walker's Critical Pronouncing Dictionary, not Hunt. Score unchanged.

title: Lake Light (weekly newspaper)
author: W. W. Phelps (publisher, with R. M. Bloomer)
evidence: Published at Trumansburg, Tompkins County, N.Y., about 50 miles from Palmyra, 1827-1828; 42 issues survive and are in this repo. Regional publication documented; no evidence of copies in Palmyra/Manchester. Grunder (MP p. 688) notes Phelps moved from the Lake Light to Canandaigua in 1828.

title: Ontario Phoenix (weekly newspaper)
author: W. W. Phelps (publisher, with R. M. Bloomer 1828-1829)
evidence: Published at Canandaigua, the Ontario County seat about 9 miles from the Smith farm, from 1828. Local publication documented by the NYS Library union list (OCLC 06586477). Not digitized; only about twenty scattered pre-1830 issues survive, so it cannot enter the analysis. Grunder (MP p. 688, citing a standard bibliography of anti-Masonic newspapers) dates Phelps & Bloomer's Ontario Phoenix from 30 Apr 1828, Bloomer leaving 16 Dec 1829.
